newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 13 pct - Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 13 pct - Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in February is expected to fall by 13 percent to 502,000 tonnes from January, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Friday.
He has previously projected a fall of 21 percent.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of February at 670,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 696,272 tonnes at end-January.
Exports in February are estimated at 440,000 tonnes.

Wong said in a report that crude palm oil (CPO) production staged a robust recovery in last-half February after dropping some 40 percent in first-half because of fewer working days arising from the double festive holidays.
"The speedy recovery was greatly assisted by good to excellent weather conditions in Peninsular Malaysia during the month," Wong said.
Plantations in East Malaysia were, however, less fortunate as widespread excessive rains during the second half of February further delayed harvesting operations, he said.
"Not only did production in East Malaysia suffered big double-digit declines, many mills also faced high FFA problems in having to process over-ripe fruits," Wong added.
Exports, in contrast, turned to be less than expected.
This shortfall was caused mainly by vessels delays, he said, adding that poor processing margins faced by refineries also contributed to the lacklustre export performance in February.
